Subject: POC traffic model + evaluation plan — owners & next steps

Hi Riley / Opsquared team — thanks again for today's call. Quick recap and proposed plan so we can get the POC kicked off next week. Please read and confirm or correct any numbers/owners.

TL;DR (ask): If you can confirm the traffic sample file and the two success criteria below by EOD Thursday, we'll provision a dedicated trial slot and share a signed mutual action plan (MAP).

Traffic profile (from call / please confirm):
- Average RPS (steady): 18 rps
- Peak RPS (burst): 140 rps for ~45s every 10 min during business hours (simulated batch jobs)
- Typical prompt lengths: 40-120 tokens (user prompt), expected generation ~120-350 tokens per request
- Concurrent sessions requiring context: 120 simultaneous chat sessions with per-session KV cache reuse
- Common batch pattern: short throughput spikes when weekly analytics jobs run (see sample)

Success criteria (proposed):
1) Latency: 95th percentile generation latency <= 320ms for <150-token outputs and <= 750ms for outputs >250 tokens under steady-state load
2) Cost: Token unit cost at or below the projected threshold in the attached PO C model (see "poc-eval-plan.xlsx") while preserving above quality bar (BLEU/ROUGE-ish internal metric target >0.78 vs baseline)

Evaluation plan & timeline:
- Wed 19 May: Opsquared to upload traffic sample (opsquared-traffic-sample.jsonl) to shared Drive; Redwood will validate profile and produce exact load schedule
- Thu 20 May: Redwood provisions trial environment (dedicated slot) and shares access + prompts/agent hooks
- Mon 24 May — Thu 27 May: 4-day trial execution window (full-run with bursts), daily syncs at 16:00 PT
- Fri 28 May: Trial wrap, metrics report, and decision checkpoint

Owners & roles:
- Opsquared owner (traffic + acceptance): Riley Thomas (riley@opsquared.com)
- Redwood technical lead (runtime & infra): Dev Patel (dev@redwoodinference.com)
- Redwood engagement lead (success criteria & contract items): Ava Chen (ava@redwoodinference.com)
- Procurement / contract POC: Marissa Cole (marissa@redwoodinference.com)

Attachments: poc-eval-plan.xlsx (workbook: trial assumptions & cost model), opsquared-traffic-sample.jsonl (sample lines attached to this thread)

Next actions (please):
- Riley: confirm traffic numbers and attach final sample to Drive by Thu EOD
- Marissa: flag any procurement/PO requirements early so we don't delay start
- Dev: validate capacity plan and confirm whether prefix caching needs special config for chat sessions

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.

Best,
Ava Chen

Thanks Ava — that summary looks right. A few clarifications and confirmations from our side:

- Confirmed: steady 18 rps, periodic peaks ~140 rps for short bursts. The spikes come from internal analytics jobs (they cluster on the 10-min marks).
- Token lengths: yes, user prompts average ~80 tokens; generated tokens vary widely but average ~220 in our historical runs. We'll include a higher-percentile tail in the sample.
- Concurrency: 120 simultaneous chat sessions is accurate during peak business hours. We'll also include a backoff pattern when users drop off.

We uploaded a 1k-line sample to the Drive folder (opsquared-traffic-sample.jsonl). It's redacted for PII but representative. Link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1opsample123/view

On success criteria: we're comfortable with the latency buckets you proposed. For cost, Opsquared's procurement wants a 3rd-party billing estimate before final sign-off (Marissa — can you loop legal/procurement contacts after the MAP?).

Timelines: Opsquared confirms EOD Thu for final sample verification. If Redwood can provision on Thu as proposed we'll start the run Monday. Can you also confirm whether model fallbacks will be enabled (e.g., switch to a smaller quantized model during sustained high load) and whether that changes the success criteria?

Thanks — Riley
